newsitem.title: UK: Russia's Dubinin sees inflation under more control.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Dubinin sees inflation under more control.

text.p: Sergei Dubinin, Russia's central bank chairman, said on Tuesday there was reason to say inflation in Russia was under control.
Speaking at a conference in London, Dubinin said, "There is reason to say now that inflation in the Russian economy is under control.
He added, "Inflation in the consumer sector fell from 131 percent in 1995 to 21.8 percent in 1996, an all-time low level since the beginning of the reform."
Dubinin said preliminary data showed consumer prices rose by a monthly average of 1.8 percent in January to March.
Dubinin said that from 1995 to 1996 production decline slowed and stable output was registered in the power, food, fuel and metallurgy sectors.
According to official statistics, at the beginning of 1997 GDP has tended towards growth compared with the same period last year, he said, and from January to February growth was 0.5 percent.
"These signs of stabilisation are to a great extent the result of the monetary policy pursued in the preceding years in order to reduce radically the inflation rate," he said.
"The Bank of Russia believes that this policy has created realistic opportunities for the accumulation of savings by all economic agents and their transformation into productive investments."
